paragraphs: Artivion, Inc. ("Artivion," the "Company," "we," or "us"), is a leader in the manufacturing, processing, and distribution of medical devices and implantable human tissues used in cardiac and vascular surgical procedures for patients with aortic disease. We have four major product families: aortic stent grafts, On-X® mechanical heart valves and related surgical products ("On-X" products), surgical sealants, and implantable cardiac and vascular human tissues. Aortic stent grafts include aortic arch stent grafts, abdominal stent grafts, and synthetic vascular grafts. Aortic arch stent grafts include our E-vita® Open NEO, E-vita Open Plus, Arcevo™ LSA Hybrid Stent Graft System ("Arcevo LSA"), the Ascyrus Medical Dissection Stent ("AMDS") hybrid prosthesis, the NEXUS ONETM ("NEXUS ONE"), NEXUS DUOTM ("NEXUS DUO"), and NEXUS TRETM ("NEXUS TRE") aortic arch stent graft systems (the "NEXUS family of products"), and E-vita Thoracic 3G products. Abdominal stent grafts include our E-xtra Design Engineering, E-nsideTM, ArtivexTM, E-tegraTM, E-ventusTM BX, TuvaTM BX, and E-liacTM products. Surgical sealants include BioGlue® Surgical Adhesive ("BioGlue") products. In addition to these four major product families, we sell or distribute PhotoFix® bovine surgical patches ("PhotoFix") and CardioGenesis® cardiac laser therapy (prior to our abandonment of the business as of June 30, 2023). We began to manufacture and supply PerClot® hemostatic powder ("PerClot") during the second quarter of 2023 (as part of the Transitional Manufacturing and Supply Agreement ("TMSA") of the Baxter Transaction).

Our main operating subsidiaries include JOTEC GmbH ("JOTEC"), a Hechingen, Germany-based endovascular and surgical products company acquired on December 1, 2017, On-X Life Technologies, Inc. ("On-X LTI"), an Austin, Texas-based mechanical heart valve company acquired on January 20, 2016, Ascyrus Medical GmbH, a manufacturing entity acquired in September 2020, as well as approximately twenty additional country entities to provide sales and marketing support throughout the world.

We have two reportable segments organized according to our products and services: Medical Devices and Preservation Services. The Medical Devices segment includes revenues from sales of aortic stent grafts, surgical sealants, On-X products, and other product revenues. The Preservation Services segment includes services revenues from the preservation of cardiac and vascular implantable human tissues. See Part II, Item 8, Note 16 of the "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements" for further information on our segments and geographic information.

Artivion is committed to partnering with surgeons and cardiologists to deliver innovative technologies of unsurpassed quality that restore the health of patients with aortic disease. Our strategic plan is focused on four growth areas that we expect to drive our business in the future as follows:
•New Products – Through product development and commercialization of new and next-generation products and services focused on aortic repair;
•New Indications – Through regulatory approvals in new markets and for new products, and through approvals for expanded indications for our existing products and services;

•Global Expansion – By entering new international markets, establishing new international direct sales territories, and developing our commercial infrastructure in new markets, including emerging markets, such as China and Brazil; and

•Business Development – By pursuing select acquisitions, licensing, and distribution opportunities that are aligned to our objectives and complement our existing products, services, and infrastructure. Examples include our acquisitions of JOTEC, On-X LTI, and Ascyrus Medical LLC ("Ascyrus"), and our distribution agreement and purchase option for the NEXUS family of products. To the extent that we identify, develop, or acquire non-core products or applications, we may dispose of these assets or pursue licensing or distribution agreements with third-party partners for development or commercialization such as the sale of the PerClot product line.

Our medical devices and preservation services are primarily used by cardiac and vascular surgeons to treat patients with aortic disease, including heart valve disease, aortic aneurysms and dissections, and, to a lesser extent, other conditions in cardiac and vascular surgery.

We face competition from several domestic and international medical device, pharmaceutical, and biopharmaceutical companies and from both for-profit and non-profit tissue processors. Many of our current and potential competitors have greater financial and personnel resources than we have. Some of these competitors might have greater experience in developing products, procuring tissues, conducting clinical trials, and obtaining regulatory approvals, and they might have contracts with large hospital groups under which they can obtain purchase requirements that place our products at a disadvantage. Some of these competitors might obtain patent protection or approval or clearance by the FDA or foreign regulators sooner than we do. Some might have superior manufacturing efficiency, tissue processing capacity, and/or marketing capabilities. We cannot ensure that our current or future competitors will not succeed in developing alternative technologies, products, or services that have advantages over those that have been, or are being, developed by us or that would render our products or technologies obsolete or non-competitive. Any of these competitive disadvantages could materially, adversely affect us.
We discuss the disease states in which we compete and our products, services, and technologies that treat these diseases below.

Patients with heart disease can experience valve insufficiency, regurgitation, or stenosis that may require heart valve repair or replacement surgery. Patients with congenital cardiac defects such as Tetralogy of Fallot, truncus arteriosus, and pulmonary atresia can require complex cardiac reconstructive surgery to repair the defect. A variety of tissues and synthetic materials are implanted in these cardiac procedures. Implantable human tissues (allografts) and animal tissues (xenografts) as well as other synthetic materials may be used in cardiac procedures. Implantable devices may be entirely synthetic, such as mechanical heart valves, or contain both synthetic materials and xenograft tissue components, such as bioprosthetic heart valves. These devices may be implanted surgically through open heart surgery, or in some cases, without sternotomy through transcatheter valve replacement.

Mechanical heart valves are durable and often last for the remainder of a patient's life without replacement, even for relatively young patients with long life expectancies. Mechanical heart valves are readily available and are a less expensive solution for those requiring a heart valve replacement. Patients who receive mechanical heart valves are required to undergo long-term blood thinning or anticoagulation drug therapy to minimize the risk of thromboembolism, stroke, or other complications from the formation of blood clots.

Bioprosthetic heart valves are readily available and are a relatively inexpensive solution for those requiring a valve replacement. Bioprosthetic heart valves contain bovine, equine, or porcine tissues that are typically processed with glutaraldehyde, which may result in progressive calcification, or hardening of the tissue over time, reducing the lifespan of the device. Bioprosthetic heart valves usually have a life of 7 to 15 years, after which the valve typically must be replaced. Patients receiving a bioprosthetic heart valve may not require long-term anticoagulation drug therapy, although some of these patients may require anticoagulation drug therapy for other heart or vascular conditions that are common in this patient population.

paragraphs: Our business involves a variety of risks and uncertainties, known and unknown, including, among others, the risks discussed below. These risks should be carefully considered together with the other information provided in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in our other filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). Our failure to adequately anticipate or address these risks and uncertainties may have a material, adverse impact on our business, reputation, revenues, financial condition, profitability, and cash flows. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known or knowable to us, or that we currently believe to be immaterial, may also adversely affect our business.
Our international operations subject us to a number of risks, which may vary significantly from the risks we face in our US operations, including:

•Greater difficulties and costs associated with staffing at all levels, establishing and maintaining internal controls, managing foreign operations and distributor relationships, and selling directly to customers;

•Broader exposure to corruption and expanded compliance obligations, including under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the UK Bribery Law, local anti-corruption laws, Office of Foreign Asset Control administered sanction programs, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation and Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, and other emerging corruption, sustainability, and data privacy and cybersecurity regulations;
•Overlapping, ambiguous, and potentially conflicting, or unexpected changes in, international legal and regulatory requirements or reimbursement policies and programs;
•Longer and more expensive collection cycles in certain countries, particularly those in which our primary customers are government-funded hospitals;

Artivion, Inc. ("Artivion," the "Company," "we," or "us"), is a leader in the manufacturing, processing, and distribution of medical devices and implantable human tissues used in cardiac and vascular surgical procedures for patients with aortic disease. We have four major product families: aortic stent grafts, On-X mechanical heart valves and related surgical products, surgical sealants, and implantable cardiac and vascular human tissues. Aortic stent grafts include aortic arch stent grafts, abdominal stent grafts, and synthetic vascular grafts. Aortic arch stent grafts include our E-vita Open NEO, E-vita Open Plus, Arcevo LSA, AMDS, NEXUS ONE, NEXUS DUO, and NEXUS TRE, and E-vita Thoracic 3G products. Abdominal stent grafts include our E-xtra Design Engineering, E-nside, Artivex, E-tegra, E-ventus BX, Tuva BX, and E-liac products. Surgical sealants include BioGlue Surgical Adhesive ("BioGlue") products. In addition to these four major product families, we sell or distribute PhotoFix bovine surgical patches ("PhotoFix") and CardioGenesis cardiac laser therapy (prior to our abandonment of that business as of June 2023). We began to manufacture and supply PerClot® hemostatic powder ("PerClot") during the second quarter of 2023 (as part of the Transitional Manufacturing and Supply Agreement ("TMSA") of the Baxter Transaction, described below).

For the year ended December 31, 2025 we reported annual revenues of $441.3 million, increasing 14% over the prior year. Excluding the effects of foreign exchange, revenues increased 13% over the prior year. The increase in revenues was due to increases in revenues from aortic stent grafts, On-X products, and surgical sealants, partially offset by a decrease in revenues from other products and preservation services, and certain limited impacts resulting from the Cybersecurity incident. For the year ended December 31, 2025 we reported a net income of $9.8 million. See the "Results of Operations" section below for additional analysis of the full year 2025 results. See Part I, Item 1, "Business," for further discussion of our business and activities during 2025.

A summary of our significant accounting policies is included in Part II, Item 8, Note 1 of the "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements." We believe that the consistent application of these policies enables us to provide users of the financial statements with useful and reliable information about our operating results and financial condition. The consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the US, which require us to make estimates and assumptions. The following are accounting policies that we believe are most important to the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations and may involve a higher degree of judgment and complexity.

Deferred preservation costs include costs of cardiac and vascular tissues available for shipment, tissues currently in active processing, and tissues held in quarantine pending release to implantable status. By federal law, human tissues cannot be bought or sold; therefore, the tissues we preserve are not held as inventory. The costs we incur to procure and process cardiac and vascular tissues are instead accumulated and deferred. Deferred preservation costs are stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value on a first-in, first-out basis and are deferred until revenue is recognized. Upon shipment of tissue to an implanting facility, revenue is recognized, and the related deferred preservation costs are expensed as cost of preservation services. Cost of preservation services also includes, as applicable, lower of cost or net realizable value write-downs and impairments for tissues not deemed to be recoverable, and includes, as incurred, idle facility expense, excessive spoilage, extra freight, and re-handling costs.

The calculation of deferred preservation costs involves judgment and complexity and uses the same principles as inventory costing. Donated human tissue is procured from deceased human donors by organ and tissue procurement organizations ("OPOs") and tissue banks that provide the tissue to us for processing, preservation, and distribution. Deferred preservation costs consist primarily of the procurement fees charged by the OPOs and tissue banks, direct labor and materials (including salary and fringe benefits, laboratory supplies and expenses, and freight-in charges), and indirect costs (including allocations of costs from support departments and facility allocations). Fixed production overhead costs are allocated based on actual tissue processing levels, to the extent that they are within the range of the facility's normal capacity.

These costs are then allocated among the tissues processed during the period based on cost drivers, such as the number of donors or number of tissues processed. We apply a yield estimate to all tissues in process and in quarantine to estimate the portion of tissues that will ultimately become implantable. We estimate quarantine and in process yields based on our historical yield experience with similar tissues and re-evaluate these estimates periodically. Actual yields could differ from our estimates, which could result in a change in tissues available for shipment and could increase or decrease the balance of deferred preservation costs. These changes could result in additional cost of preservation services expense or could increase per tissue preservation costs, which would impact gross margins on tissue preservation services in future periods.

We regularly evaluate our deferred preservation costs to determine if the costs are appropriately recorded at the lower of cost or net realizable value. We also evaluate our deferred preservation costs for costs not deemed to be recoverable, including tissues not expected to ship prior to the expiration date of their packaging. Lower of cost or net realizable value write-downs are recorded if the tissue processing costs incurred exceed the estimated market value of the tissue services, based on recent average service fees at the time of the evaluation. Impairment write-downs are recorded based on the book value of tissues deemed to be impaired. Actual results may differ from these estimates. Write-downs of deferred preservation costs are expensed as cost of preservation services, and these write-downs are permanent impairments that create a new cost basis, which cannot be restored to its previous levels if our estimates change.

Contingent consideration represents a recurring fair value estimate of potential future payments. The fair value of the contingent consideration liability is estimated by discounting to present value the contingent payments expected to be made based on a probability-weighted scenario approach. A discount rate is applied based on our unsecured credit spread and the term commensurate risk-free rate to the additional consideration to be paid, and then we apply a risk-based estimate of the probability of achieving each scenario to calculate the fair value of the contingent consideration. We used a discount rate of approximately 16% and estimated future achievement of milestone dates between 2025 and 2026 to calculate the fair value of contingent consideration as of December 31, 2025. This fair value measurement was based on unobservable inputs, including management estimates and assumptions about the future achievement of milestones and future estimate of revenues, and is, therefore, classified as Level 3 within the fair value hierarchy.
See Part II, Item 8, Note 1 of "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements" for further discussion of new accounting standards that have been adopted or are being evaluated for future adoption.

paragraphs: Artivion, Inc. ("Artivion," the "Company," "we," or "us"), 為醫療器材與植入式人體組織製造、加工與配送的領導者，用於治療患有主動脈疾病患者的心臟與血管手術程序。我們有四大主要產品系列：主動脈支架移植物、On-X®機械心臟瓣膜與相關手術產品（"On-X" 產品）、手術密封劑，以及植入式心臟與血管人體組織。主動脈支架移植物包括主動脈弓支架移植物、腹部支架移植物與合成血管移植物。主動脈弓支架移植物包括我們的 E-vita® Open NEO、E-vita Open Plus、Arcevo™ LSA Hybrid Stent Graft System（"Arcevo LSA"）、Ascyrus Medical Dissection Stent（"AMDS"）混合假體、NEXUS ONETM（"NEXUS ONE"）、NEXUS DUOTM（"NEXUS DUO"）、NEXUS TRETM（"NEXUS TRE"）主動脈弓支架移植物系統（"NEXUS 產品系列"），以及 E-vita Thoracic 3G 產品。腹部支架移植物包括我們的 E-xtra Design Engineering、E-nsideTM、ArtivexTM、E-tegraTM、E-ventusTM BX、TuvaTM BX、以及 E-liacTM 產品。手術密封劑包括 BioGlue® 手術黏合劑（"BioGlue"）產品。除了這四大主要產品系列，我們銷售或分銷 PhotoFix® 牛皮手術補片（"PhotoFix"）與 CardioGenesis® 心臟雷射治療（在 2023 年 6 月 30 日我們放棄該業務前）。我們於 2023 年第二季開始製造與供應 PerClot® 止血粉末（"PerClot"）（作為 Baxter 交易的過渡製造與供應協議（"TMSA"）的一部分）。

我們的主要營運子公司包括 JOTEC GmbH（"JOTEC"），一家位於德國 Hechingen 的內血管與手術產品公司，於 2017 年 12 月取得；On-X Life Technologies, Inc.（"On-X LTI"），一家位於德克薩斯州 Austin 的機械心臟瓣膜公司，於 2016 年 1 月取得；Ascyrus Medical GmbH，一家於 2020 年 9 月取得的製造機構，以及約二十個其他國家機構，用以在全球提供銷售與行銷支援。
我們有兩個應報告分部，根據我們的產品與服務進行組織：醫療器材與保存服務。醫療器材分部包括來自主動脈支架移植物、手術密封劑、On-X 產品及其他產品銷售的收入。保存服務分部包括來自心臟與血管植入式人體組織保存服務的服務收入。請參閱 "財務報表附註" 第二部分，第 8 項，第 16 節，以取得更多關於我們分部與地理資訊的資訊。
Artivion 承諾與外科醫生與心臟科醫生合作，提供創新技術，品質無與倫比，以恢復患有主動脈疾病患者的健康。我們的戰略計畫聚焦於四個成長領域，我們預期這些領域將驅動我們未來的業務發展，如下所述：
• 新產品 – 透過新產品與次世代產品與服務的開發與商業化，專注於主動脈修補；
• 新適應症 – 透過新市場與新產品的法規批准，以及現有產品與服務的擴展適應症批准；
• 全球擴張 – 透過進入新國際市場、建立新國際直接銷售區域，並在新市場（包括中國與巴西等新興市場）發展我們的商業基礎設施；以及

• 商業發展 – 透過追求符合我們目標且與現有產品、服務與基礎設施補充的特定收購、授權與分銷機會。範例包括我們收購 JOTEC、On-X LTI 與 Ascyrus Medical LLC（"Ascyrus"），以及我們的 NEXUS 產品系列分銷協議與購買選擇權。在我們識別、開發或收購非核心產品或應用程序的情況下，我們可能會處置這些資產，或與第三方合作夥伴簽訂授權或分銷協議，以進行開發或商業化，例如 PerClot 產品線的銷售。
本公司之醫療器材與保存服務主要用於心臟外科與血管外科手術師治療患有主動脈疾病之病患，包括心臟瓣膜疾病、主動脈瘤與主動脈剝離，以及較少見之其他心臟與血管外科手術狀況。

我們面臨來自數家國內與國際醫療器材、藥品與生物製藥公司，以及營利與非營利組織之組織處理者的競爭。許多我們現有或潛在之競爭對手擁有較我們更優渥之財務與人力資源。部分競爭對手可能在產品開發、取得組織、進行臨牀試驗與取得監管核准方面擁有較豐富之經驗，且可能與大型醫院羣體簽訂契約，使其能取得採購需求，而使我們之產品處於劣勢。部分競爭對手可能比我們更早取得美國食品藥物管理局或外國監管機構之專利保護或核准。部分競爭對手可能擁有更優越之製造效率、組織處理能力與/或市場推廣能力。我們無法確保現有或未來之競爭對手不會成功開發出具有優勢之替代技術、產品或服務，或使我們之產品或技術過時或失去競爭力。任何這些競爭劣勢都可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
我們在以下段落中說明我們競爭之疾病狀態以及我們用以治療這些疾病之產品、服務與技術。

患有心臟疾病之病患可能經歷瓣膜不全、反流或狹窄，可能需要進行心臟瓣膜修補或置換手術。患有先天性心臟缺陷如法洛四聯症、主動脈幹與肺動脈閉鎖之病患可能需要進行複雜之心臟重建手術以修復缺陷。這些心臟手術中會植入多種組織與合成材料。植入式人體組織（異體組織）與動物組織（異種組織）以及其他合成材料可能用於心臟手術中。植入式裝置可能是完全合成的，如機械性心臟瓣膜，或包含合成材料與異種組織零組件，如生物性心臟瓣膜。這些裝置可能透過開胸手術植入，或在某些情況下，不需開胸透過經導管瓣膜置換方式植入。
機械性心臟瓣膜耐用且通常可維持病患餘生而無需更換，即使對於預期壽命較長之年輕病患亦然。機械性心臟瓣膜容易取得，且為需要心臟瓣膜置換之病患提供較廉價之解決方案。接受機械性心臟瓣膜之病患需長期服用抗凝血或抗凝藥物以降低血栓栓塞、中風或其他因血塊形成所致併發症之風險。

生物性心臟瓣膜容易取得，且為需要瓣膜置換之病患提供相對廉價之解決方案。生物性心臟瓣膜包含牛、馬或豬之組織，通常經 glutaraldehyde 處理，可能導致組織逐漸鈣化或硬化，降低裝置之使用壽命。生物性心臟瓣膜通常使用壽命為 7 至 15 年，之後通常需更換。接受生物性心臟瓣膜之病患可能無需長期服用抗凝血藥物，不過部分病患可能因其他心臟或血管疾病而需服用抗凝血藥物，這些疾病在該病患族羣中相當常見。

paragraphs: 下列有關我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論應配合我們合併財務報表及相關附註，並包含於本檔其他部分。討論中包含前瞻性陳述，涉及已知及未知的風險與不確定性，包括於本表10-K第一部分第1A項「風險因素」所列者。下列討論與分析未包含與2023年12月31日結業年度相關的某些項目，包括2024年12月31日結業年度與2023年12月31日結業年度的年對年比較。如需比較我們2024年12月31日結業年度與2023年12月31日結業年度的營運成果，請參閱我們2024年12月31日結業年度的年度報告表10-K，該報告於2025年2月28日提交至SEC。

Artivion, Inc. ("Artivion," the "Company," "we," or "us"), 是製造、加工與分銷用於心臟及血管手術程序的醫療器材與植入式人體組織的領導者，適用於患有主動脈疾病的患者。我們有四大主要產品系列：主動脈支架移植物、On-X機械心瓣膜及相關手術產品、手術密封劑，以及植入式心臟及血管人體組織。主動脈支架移植物包括主動脈弓支架移植物、腹部支架移植物及合成血管移植物。主動脈弓支架移植物包括我們的 E-vita Open NEO、E-vita Open Plus、Arcevo LSA、AMDS、NEXUS ONE、NEXUS DUO、NEXUS TRE，以及 E-vita Thoracic 3G 產品。腹部支架移植物包括我們的 E-xtra Design Engineering、E-nside、Artivex、E-tegra、E-ventus BX、Tuva BX，以及 E-liac 產品。手術密封劑包括 BioGlue Surgical Adhesive ("BioGlue") 產品。除了這四大主要產品系列，我們銷售或分銷 PhotoFix 牛類手術貼片 ("PhotoFix") 以及 CardioGenesis 心臟雷射治療 (在2023年6月我們放棄該業務前)。我們於2023年第二季開始製造與供應 PerClot® 止血粉末 ("PerClot") (為 Baxter 交易中所述的過渡製造與供應協議 ("TMSA") 的一部分)。
我們重要的會計政策摘要包含於第二部分第8項，附註1的「合併財務報表附註」。我們認為這些政策的一致應用，使財務報表使用者能獲得有關我們營運成果與財務狀況的有用且可靠資訊。合併財務報表係依照美國通用會計準則 (GAAP) 進行編製，這要求我們做出估計與假設。以下為我們認為對呈現我們財務狀況與營運成果最重要，且可能涉及較高程度判斷與複雜性的會計政策。

遞延保存成本包括可運送的心臟與血管組織成本、目前正在處理中的組織成本，以及待釋放為植入狀態的組織成本。根據聯邦法律，人體組織不得買賣；因此，我們保存的組織並未作為存貨持有。我們為取得與處理心臟與血管組織所產生的成本，則會累積並遞延。遞延保存成本以先進先出方式，按成本與淨可實現價值較低者計列，並遞延至收入確認時點。組織運送至植入設施時，確認收入，並將相關遞延保存成本計入保存服務成本。保存服務成本亦包括，如適用，按成本與淨可實現價值較低者計列的寫跌價與減損，以及如發生，閒置設施費用、過度損耗、額外運費與重新處理費用。

遞延保存成本的計算涉及判斷與複雜性，並使用與存貨計價相同的原則。捐贈人體組織由器官與組織取得組織機構 ("OPOs") 及組織銀行取得，這些機構將組織提供給我們進行處理、保存與分銷。遞延保存成本主要由 OPOs 及組織銀行收取的取得費用、直接人工與材料 (包括薪資與福利、實驗室用品與費用，以及運費) 及間接成本 (包括支援部門成本的分攤與設施分攤) 組成。固定生產間接費用根據實際組織處理量進行分攤，以不超出設施正常容量範圍為限。

這些成本隨後根據成本驅動因素，如捐贈人數或處理組織數量，分攤至當期處理的組織。我們對所有處理中及待處理組織應用產出率估計，以估計最終能成為植入物的組織比例。我們根據歷史經驗，以類似組織的產出率估計待處理及處理中組織的產出率，並定期重新評估這些估計。實際產出率可能與我們的估計不同，這可能導致可運送組織數量的變動，並可能增加或減少遞延保存成本的餘額。這些變動可能導致保存服務成本增加，或增加每單位組織的保存成本，進而影響未來期間組織保存服務的毛利率。

我們定期評估遞延保存成本，以確認其是否正確計列為成本與淨可實現價值較低者。我們亦評估遞延保存成本，以確認是否不具可收回性，包括預期在包裝過期前無法運送的組織。若組織處理成本高於評估時點的近期平均服務費用所估計的組織服務市場價值，則會計入成本與淨可實現價值較低者寫跌價。減損寫跌價則根據被認為減損的組織帳面價值計列。實際結果可能與這些估計不同。遞延保存成本的寫跌價計入保存服務成本，且這些寫跌價為永久減損，一旦我們的估計變動，無法恢復至原先水平。

Contingent consideration 代表潛在未來付款之公平價值之重複評估。 contingent consideration liability 之公平價值係透過將預期將支付之 contingent payments 以機率加權情境法折現至現值來估算。 折現率係根據本公司無擔保信用利差及與額外考慮支付金額相應之無風險利率來計算，然後我們應用基於風險之情境達成機率之估計，以計算 contingent consideration 之公平價值。 我們使用約 16% 之折現率，並估計未來達成里程碑日期於 2025 年至 2026 年之間，以計算 2025 年 12 月 31 日 contingent consideration 之公平價值。 此公平價值衡量係基於不可觀察之輸入資料，包括管理層對未來達成里程碑及未來收入之估計與假設，因此被歸類為公平價值階層中之 Level 3。

headings: 風險與我們的業務相關
我們因國際業務運作及持續的全球擴張而面臨多種風險。
我們經營在高度競爭的市場區段，面臨來自大型、具備豐富資源的醫療器材公司及組織服務供應商的競爭，我們可能無法有效競爭。
我們的收入大幅依賴於組織保存服務，並面臨影響這些收入的多種風險。
我們的收入大幅依賴於BioGlue產品，並面臨與之相關的多種風險。
我們的收入大幅依賴於主動脈支架移植物，並面臨與之相關的多種風險。
我們的收入大幅依賴於On-X產品，並面臨與之相關的多種風險。
外幣相對於美元的持續波動可能對我們的業務造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司部分產品與技術可能面臨重大智慧財產權風險與不確定性。
公共衛生危機已對本公司產生重大不利影響，並可能持續產生，甚至未來也可能產生重大不利影響。
本公司嚴重依賴供應商與委外製造商提供具備品質之產品。
本公司依賴單一來源供應商與單一廠區。
本公司依賴具專業技術之員工羣。
本公司持續評估透過收購、授權、投資與其他公司或技術之分銷協議進行擴張，此等行動可能伴隨重大風險。
本公司因收購、資產處分、合作夥伴關係及其他業務發展活動所產生之費用，可能對本公司普通股之市場價值產生重大不利影響。
本公司可能無法實現所有預期之業務發展活動效益。
資訊科技系統的重大中斷或資訊安全系統的違規事件可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司業務可能受到環境、人力資源及治理相關事項的影響。
本公司產品及組織皆屬高度管制，並面臨顯著的品質與法規風險。
美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）對 CryoValve SG 肺動脈心臟瓣膜（"CryoValve SGPV"）的重新分類，可能使繼續處理 CryoValve SGPV 在商業上不可行。
本公司可能無法成功取得新產品及既有產品與服務的臨牀結果或法規核准/批准，且本公司已核准之產品與服務可能無法獲得市場接受。
針對本公司產業所使用之製程與材料，環境法規的加強及私人訴訟活動增加，可能對本公司產生重大且不利的影響。
本公司若被認為促進未核准或非標籤用途之產品使用，可能面臨罰款、處罰及其他制裁。

paragraphs: 本公司業務涉及多種風險與不確定性，包括已知與未知的風險，例如下列所討論的風險。這些風險應與本年度10-K表報表及其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的文件中提供的資訊一併仔細考量。本公司若未能充分預見或處理這些風險與不確定性，可能對本公司業務、聲譽、營業收入、財務狀況、獲利能力及現金流產生重大且不利的影響。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或無法預測，或目前認為不重要，也可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司國際業務使我們面臨多種風險，這些風險可能與我們在美國業務所面臨的風險有顯著差異，包括：
•在各層級聘僱人手的困難與成本增加、建立與維持內部控制、管理海外業務與經銷商關係，以及直接向客戶銷售的困難與成本增加；
•更廣泛的貪腐風險與擴大的合規義務，包括根據《美國反貪污法》、英國貪污法、當地反貪腐法規、財產管制辦公室（OFAC）管理的制裁計畫、歐盟《一般資料保護規則》與《企業永續發展報告指令》，以及其他新興的貪腐、永續發展與資料隱私及網路安全規範；
•國際法律與法規要求或報銷政策與計畫的重疊、模糊，或可能衝突，或出乎預料的變更；
•某些國家的帳款回收週期較長且成本較高，特別是在主要客戶為政府資助醫院的國家。
